jobs.title: Sr. Business & Portfolio Strategy Analyst
jobs.description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.
Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

About the Opportunity

We are seeking an exceptional emerging strategy professional to help shape the future of a >$3B global consumer electronics business.
Our business spans the full consumer value chain—from consumer insights, product strategy, design, and development through marketing, sales, and supply chain. This creates a unique opportunity to influence both long-term business direction and the product portfolio choices that drive growth and profitability.
This role is ideal for someone who combines structured strategic thinking, exceptional written communication, analytical curiosity, and a highly collaborative working style.

The successful candidate will be comfortable starting with an ambiguous business question, working across functions to define the problem, developing frameworks and hypotheses, and identifying the data and insights needed to test potential solutions. Equally important, they must be able to distill complex strategies and analyses into clear, persuasive written narratives that support decisions at the executive and Board of Directors level.
We are particularly interested in candidates with a foundation in top-tier management consulting who are eager to move from advising businesses to directly influencing strategic choices and outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Problem Framing & Hypothesis Development
Lead the structured definition of complex, often ambiguous business problems, translating broad strategic questions into clear issues, analytical frameworks, and testable hypotheses.
Collaborate closely with functional leaders and subject matter experts to develop an understanding of the business, challenge assumptions, and identify the most important questions to answer.
Apply hypothesis-driven problem-solving techniques to focus analytical efforts on the highest-impact issues.
Identify relevant internal and external data sources, determine what evidence is needed, and develop practical approaches to testing hypotheses.
Synthesize quantitative and qualitative findings, refining hypotheses as new information emerges.
Balance analytical rigor with pragmatism, recognizing when sufficient evidence exists to support a strategic recommendation.
Executive Communication & Strategic Storytelling
Translate complex strategic thinking, business analyses, and cross-functional inputs into concise, compelling written narratives for senior executives and the Board of Directors.
Develop high-quality strategy memoranda, executive briefs, decision papers, and strategic recommendations that make complicated issues easy to understand.
Structure communications around clear conclusions, supporting evidence, strategic implications, and decisions required.
Distill large amounts of information into the essential insights, trade-offs, and recommendations without losing critical nuance.
Tailor communications to different audiences, from working-level teams to executive leadership and the Board.
Establish a high standard for clarity, precision, logical flow, and persuasive business writing.
Business Unit & Product Portfolio Strategy
Support development of the business unit's multi-year strategy, including growth opportunities, competitive positioning, market priorities, and investment choices.
Partner with Product Management, Consumer Insights, Finance, and other functions to develop and refine product portfolio strategies.
Evaluate consumer needs, market dynamics, competitive trends, product economics, and portfolio performance to inform strategic decisions.
Develop business cases and strategic scenarios to evaluate growth opportunities, portfolio alternatives, and resource allocation.
Connect product portfolio recommendations to broader business objectives, financial performance, and long-term competitive advantage.
Collaborative Discovery & Cross-Functional Engagement
Build trusted relationships across Product Management, Design, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Finance, and Supply Chain.
Approach new strategic challenges with curiosity, humility, and a genuine desire to learn from those closest to the business.
Facilitate working sessions that bring structure to complex discussions, surface diverse perspectives, and establish shared understanding of problems and opportunities.
Work collaboratively with subject matter experts to identify relevant information, test assumptions, and develop fact-based conclusions.
Constructively challenge existing thinking while remaining open to alternative perspectives and new evidence.
Build alignment and influence decisions through strong reasoning, credibility, and collaboration rather than positional authority.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Finance, or a related discipline.
Typically 2–5 years of experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, or a similarly rigorous analytical environment.
Outstanding written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to translate complex business issues into concise, logically structured, executive-ready memoranda and recommendations.
Strong command of structured problem-solving methodologies, including issue definition, analytical frameworks, hypothesis development, and hypothesis testing.
Demonstrated resourcefulness in identifying, gathering, and analyzing data to answer complex business questions, including situations where information is incomplete or difficult to access.
Ability to synthesize qualitative and quantitative information into actionable strategic insights.
Highly collaborative working style, strong listening skills, intellectual humility, and the ability to learn quickly from cross-functional experts.
Strong business judgment, intellectual curiosity, and comfort navigating ambiguity.

Preferred

Experience at a leading strategy consulting firm such as McKinsey, Bain, BCG, or a comparable organization.
Experience developing executive-level strategy documents, investment recommendations, or Board-facing materials.
Exposure to consumer electronics, technology, consumer products, or other innovation-driven businesses.
Experience in growth strategy, product portfolio strategy, corporate strategy, or commercial due diligence.
MBA or advanced degree is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will:
Bring clarity and structure to ambiguous strategic questions, helping leadership focus on the issues that matter most.
Build effective partnerships with business leaders and functional experts, demonstrating curiosity and credibility during the discovery process.
Develop thoughtful, evidence-based hypotheses and know how to efficiently find the information needed to validate or challenge them.
Produce exceptionally clear strategy memoranda that enable executives and Board members to quickly understand complex issues, evaluate trade-offs, and make informed decisions.
Contribute meaningfully to business unit and product portfolio strategies that influence long-term growth and competitiveness.

At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $149,500-$205,600.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves.

jobs.title: Data Analyst/Scientist or Senior Data Analyst/Scientist
jobs.description:
Bristol or London

About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, an electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

About The Role

Our multi-disciplinary software, product, and data team serves as a central hub of digital expertise and innovation, supporting projects across the company. We work collaboratively with engineers, consultants and other specialists to use data and technology to solve real-world problems and improve the services we provide to our clients.

We have an opportunity for a Data Analyst/Scientist or Senior Data Analyst/Scientist to play a key role in using data, analytics, statistical methods and data science to generate insight, support decision-making and improve our engineering services.

This is a broad analytical role. You will work across the full lifecycle of a problem: understanding stakeholder needs, exploring and assessing data, identifying appropriate analytical approaches, communicating findings and, where appropriate, developing statistical or machine-learning models or client-ready insights/tools. This is a role for someone who enjoys variety and has a critical eye for finding the right solution for the problem. Sometimes this may be exploratory analysis, a dashboard or a set of clearly defined metrics; in other cases, it may involve forecasting, statistical modelling, machine learning or building/working with AI.

It's an exciting time to join our Digital team. Working alongside a range of specialist engineers and consultants, you will be joining a collaborative, knowledgeable, highly engaged team, and offer a supportive, flexible, and high-performing work culture. In a time where building and energy resilience is ever more important, we are driving forward innovation to make an impact with data and technology.

You will have the opportunity to engage in a variety of high-impact projects, working on challenging problems for some of the UK’s most notable organisations, including the NHS and Oxford University. Our team has recently worked on creating data science-led for managing estates in hospitals, building energy forecasting models, and harnessing data on building performance to create better designed buildings of the future.

In this key and varied role, you can expect to:

Work with engineers, consultants, product teams and other stakeholders to understand their needs and translate sometimes ambiguous questions into well-defined analytical problems.
Develop and implement data-driven solutions to solve real-world business problems across the company.
Use SQL, Python and other analytical tools to investigate datasets, identify trends and relationships, test hypotheses and generate actionable insights.
Apply appropriate statistical techniques, forecasting methods, ML and AI approaches where they add value to the problem being solved.
Collaborate with the product and software engineering teams to turn analytical work into reusable tools, workflows and data-driven products where appropriate.
Develop reproducible and maintainable analytical code, following best practices, including version control, testing, and peer reviews.
Contribute to the development of analytical and data science capability across the business by sharing approaches, reusable methods and good practice

About You

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

Essential Skills

Experience applying data and analysis to real-world business, engineering or operational problems.
Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to take an initially ambiguous question and determine an appropriate analytical approach.
Ability to work on projects independently and own deliverables.
Strong proficiency in Python for data manipulation, analysis, visualisation and data science (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn).
Proficiency in data querying languages (e.g., SQL). Solid understanding of software engineering best practices (version control, unit testing, code review, etc.).
Strong experience with data visualisation frameworks (e.g., PowerBI, Streamlit).
Experience applying machine learning and AI, including generative AI, to real-world problems where it provides clear benefit.
Familiarity with statistical concepts and their application in data analysis.
Solid communication skills, capable of effectively engaging with and presenting findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Understanding of data governance, privacy, responsible AI and other relevant standards.

Desirable Skills

Knowledge of the engineering industry and its challenges.
Experience with one of the major machine learning frameworks (TensorFlow or PyTorch).
Knowledge of mathematical optimisation methods, such as linear, integer or constraint optimisation, and associated tools (e.g. OR-Tools).
Experience with MS Fabric or equivalent data warehousing solution.
Experience working in a cloud computing environment.
Familiarity with containerisation and deployment technologies (e.g., Docker, CI/CD pipelines).

For candidates joining at Senior
level, we would additionally expect you to lead more complex or ambiguous analytical projects, shape analytical approaches and overarching priorities, work independently with senior stakeholders, review and support the work of others, and help raise analytical standards across the team.

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application.

If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange an introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices. We aim to provide feedback at each stage of the process.

Adjustments and accommodations

If there are adjustments or accommodations that we can put in place to help you participate and give your best at any stage of the recruitment process (whether relating to disability, neurodivergence or anything else) please let us know.

jobs.description:
With all the information available today, it takes a skilled intelligence analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government and military every day, we need an intel analyst like you to do just that. As a C4I analyst, you use your specialized functional experience and attention to detail to conduct all-source analysis with an emphasis on national C4I analysis in compliance with DIA’s SOP for C4I Functional Production Area, DIA ADO, and ICD 203 or 206 standards.

Join us. The world can't wait.

Work Schedule:
This position is standard work hours

Essential Responsibilities:

As a C4I all-source intelligence analyst on our team, you’ll help your client by providing intelligence production and briefing support to address dynamic intelligence requirements. Using your comprehensive understanding of C4I and all-source analysis, you will provide C4I and telecommunications infrastructure intelligence analysis on military’s national C4I organizations, systems, processes, technologies, and telecommunications networks, identify potential vulnerabilities in redundancy, confidentiality, and system integrity, and provide support for identifying, locating, and tracking deployment of foreign mobile signal, electronic warfare, and SIGINT units that support joint or national C4I functions.

As an authority on your topic, your client will look to you for comprehensive reviews, often under pressure. This is a chance to grow your expertise and broaden your skill set in areas like analysis, writing, and communication. You’ll share your expertise with other analysts through leadership and mentoring. We focus on growing as a team to deliver the best support to our customers, so you’ll have resources to learn new skills and tools. Join us as we provide the right information at the right time to support the critical needs of our warfighters and the nation’s leaders.

Knowledge of the IC and Combatant Command environment
Ability to develop high-quality deliverables tailored to senior policymakers or defense stakeholders, including complex written products and briefings

TS/SCI

Bachelor’s degree

10+ years of experience supporting military or government planning operations in lieu of a degree

Serve as a technology and data management risk expert on committees and working groups, fostering strong internal relationships.

Work with the FLOD to provide guidance and effective challenge for operational risks assessments and collaborate with teams across the organization.

Intermediate speaking and writing communication skills.

General knowledge of industry and professional experience across one or more of the three lines of defense (e.g., compliance, risk management, information technology, or audit).

Information Security Risk Analyst London / WFH to £90k

Are you an Information Security professional with experience in risk assessment, security governance and control assurance?

You could be progressing your career in an impactful role at a tech driven, global Asset Manager with multiple billions of dollars under management.

As an Information Security Risk Analyst you'll play a key role in implementing and strengthening security risk management, helping the business make informed decisions while maintaining robust security standards in a changing regulatory and technology landscape.

You'll assess security risks across systems, projects, technology changes, AI tools and third party suppliers, translating your findings into practical recommendations and actionable risk treatment plans. You'll maintain the Information Security Risk Register, ensuring risks have clear ownership, appropriate controls and effective remediation through to closure.

You'll evaluate security controls against recognised frameworks such as ISO 27001 and NIST CSF, identify gaps and support maturity assessments to benchmark the organisation's security posture. Working closely with Security Operations and Engineering, you'll analyse monthly key risk indicators (KRIs), using threat, vulnerability and incident data to identify trends, highlight systemic weaknesses and communicate business risk.

You'll also contribute to security governance, preparing reports for risk forums and senior management, managing policy exceptions and risk acceptances and tracking decisions and actions. You'll help maintain security policies, standards and procedures, monitor evolving regulatory requirements including FCA regulation, DORA and GDPR and support internal and external audits.

You're familiar with ISO 27001, NIST CSF and relevant regulatory requirements, ideally within financial services

Overview

The Senior Data Analyst is responsible for turning CRM and marketing data into clear, defensible business decisions.

This role executes analysis with precision while identifying what is working, what is not, and where programs should adjust. This role sits at the center of delivery; ensuring data is accurate, analysis is sound, and outputs are ready to inform decisions.

You will support one of our client’s CRM programs across aftersales and retail touchpoints, working across data, analytics, and account teams to ensure programs are measurable, accurate, and improving over time. This is a high-accountability execution role. You are expected to deliver accurate analysis, surface key insights, and ensure outputs are ready to inform decisions.

Responsibilities

Core Responsibilities

Performance Measurement and Impact Validation: Ensure programs are measured correctly and results are credible

Analyze CRM performance across channels (direct mail, email, digital)
Apply structured measurement approaches (test vs control, pre/post, matched comparisons where applicable)
Identify drivers of performance; audience, offer, timing, channel
Translate findings into clear “what to do next” implications

Analysis Execution: Own the data and logic behind every output

Write and own SQL queries to extract, join, and validate data across sources
Execute recurring and ad hoc analyses for CRM programs (aftersales and retail support)
Ensure all outputs are accurate, complete, and aligned to business logic
Reproduce results consistently; no one-off logic that cannot be traced

Insight Generation: Go beyond dashboards; explain what matters

Build and maintain reporting outputs (Tableau, Excel, etc.), while highlighting key drivers, anomalies, and performance shifts
Provide clear summaries of “what happened” and “why it matters”

Data Ownership and Quality: Numbers are trusted because you validate them

Own QA/QC across datasets, queries, and final outputs
Validate campaign counts, audience definitions, and performance metrics
Identify and escalate data inconsistencies early
Ensure alignment between analytics outputs and campaign execution

Execution Support Across Teams: Operate within the system, not in isolation

Partner with campaign, account, and data teams to support program execution
Understand how data flows through systems and where issues can occur
Support data pulls, audience validation, and post-campaign analysis

Structured Problem Solving: Turn ambiguity into clear analysis quickly

Break down ambiguous requests into clear analytical steps
Investigate discrepancies and performance issues with a methodical approach
Prioritize practical answers over perfect ones when timelines require it

Communication and Deliverables: Make analysis usable

Contribute to decks, summaries, and readouts with clear, concise language
Present findings internally; support client-facing materials as needed
Focus on clarity and accuracy; avoid overcomplicating the message

Qualifications

Working Style and Characteristics

Owns the numbers end-to-end

About The Role

Charlotte, NC

Home Solutions is hiring a Senior Research Analyst
to build the insights that put us in front of the people who run home services.

You will research the biggest questions facing the top 50 to 100 home services companies and turn the answers into work their CEOs, CMOs, and CROs actually want to read. Each quarter you will pick a topic, go deep, and publish an industry report. Then you will use AI to turn that report into custom briefs for the 200 executives who matter most to our business.

Your work informs our CEO and Chief Revenue Officer as they build relationships with these leaders. You will report to our VP of GTM Strategy and work closely with our executive team. Within your first year, you will have published four quarterly reports and delivered custom briefs that open doors with top partners and prospects. You will also have built a repeatable AI workflow that turns one report into 200 tailored briefs in days, not months.

Your Day-to-Day

Run deep research using industry sources, third-party data, executive interviews, and our own data on 50M+ homeowners.
Design original research, including surveys and data studies, that produces insights no one else has.
Write a quarterly industry report with clear findings, sharp charts, and a real point of view.
Manage a backlog of topics each quarter with our Go-to-Market Strategy lead, based on the problems home services leaders are trying to solve right now.
Build profiles of the top 200 executives and their companies, covering their priorities, recent moves, and competitive pressures.
Use AI tools to turn each report into a custom brief for each executive and their business.
Build and refine the prompts, templates, and workflows that make personalization fast and repeatable.
Prep our CEO and Chief Revenue Officer for executive meetings, partner conversations, and industry events.
Recommend new data sources and research tools as the program grows.

About You

2 to 4 years of experience in research or advisory at a top firm. Strategy consulting or equity research also fits.
Experience owning the full research cycle, from framing the question to presenting findings to a senior audience.
You can run a quarterly research cycle on your own while handling requests from senior leaders.
Strong written communication with the ability to turn dense research into a clear story an executive reads and digests quickly.
You are comfortable with data. You can pull, clean, and analyze datasets in Excel or similar tools, and you know when a number does not hold up.
You use AI tools every day, have built your own workflows with them, and know how to pick the right tool for the job. Coding is not required.
You are curious about how companies grow. Interest in home services, marketing, or consumer businesses is a plus.
High ownership, low ego, and a bias toward action.

At Home Solutions, we're on a mission to build a more innovative future for home services. Since 2017, we've been transforming how homeowners and service providers connect-replacing outdated lead-generation models with a smarter, outcome-driven approach.

We combine proprietary media, AI, and deep data insights to reach 50M+ homeowners and match them with high-quality providers through seamless, high-intent experiences. Culture: We're a team that plays to win- holding a high bar for excellence while creating an environment where people enjoy the work and the people they do it with.

jobs.description:
Role Purpose

We are seeking a capable and commercially aware Project Manager with experience in ports, terminals, logistics, industrial, or related infrastructure
to manage capital projects from initial assessment through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover.
The role sits within a lean projects team and requires an individual who can take genuine ownership of projects rather than simply administer them. The successful candidate will work across technical, operational, commercial, and stakeholder interfaces and will be expected to independently drive projects while escalating key decisions, risks, and strategic issues when required.
This is a client-side project management role
. It requires sufficient technical depth to challenge consultants, contractors, and proposed solutions, while maintaining focus on programme, cost, risk, constructability, operational requirements, and business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Project Development & Feasibility

Support the assessment of new port, terminal, logistics, warehouse, depot, and infrastructure development opportunities.
Review available site information, operational requirements, surveys, existing infrastructure, utilities, access, marine constraints, and authority requirements.
Participate in site investigations and identify missing information, constraints, risks, and potential project blockers.
Develop or coordinate preliminary layouts, scope definitions, development concepts, and implementation strategies.
Prepare or review preliminary quantities, ROM CAPEX estimates
, project schedules, and development assumptions.
Challenge proposed layouts and technical solutions from the perspectives of constructability, operations, cost, phasing, and future expansion.
Contribute technical and project-delivery input to feasibility studies, business-development proposals, concessions, leases, and investment evaluations.

Design Management

Prepare consultant scopes of work, technical briefs, and design deliverable requirements.
Manage multidisciplinary consultants across relevant disciplines including civil, structural, architectural, MEP, marine, utilities, traffic, fire and life safety, and specialist systems.
Coordinate design inputs from operations, commercial, IT, equipment, HSE, maintenance, finance, and other internal stakeholders.
Review drawings, specifications, calculations, BOQs, reports, and design submissions.
Identify design gaps, interface risks, constructability issues, unnecessary cost, and scope ambiguity.
Manage design development from concept through tender and IFC stages.
Ensure designs reflect operational requirements and minimize disruption to existing port or logistics operations.

Procurement & Commercial Support

Prepare and coordinate tender packages for consultants, contractors, and specialist suppliers.
Participate in tender clarification meetings, technical evaluations, bid normalization, and recommendation reports.
Review contractor methodologies, programmes, qualifications, exclusions, and technical proposals.
Support commercial teams with scope clarification, variation assessment, change management, and contractual correspondence.
Assist with CAPEX control, commitments, forecasts, and evaluation of project cost impacts.
Maintain awareness of contractual obligations, deliverables, milestones, and project risks.

Project Execution

Take day-to-day ownership of assigned projects from award through completion.
Establish project execution plans, programmes, deliverable schedules, reporting structures, and responsibility matrices.
Coordinate consultants, contractors, suppliers, internal departments, authorities, landlords, and other stakeholders.
Monitor construction progress against approved programme, budget, scope, quality, and HSE requirements.
Lead regular project and progress meetings and drive closure of actions.
Identify delays and emerging risks early and develop mitigation or recovery measures.
Review contractor programmes, progress claims, variations, RFIs, technical submissions, and change requests.
Ensure technical decisions are made with consideration of programme, cost, operational impact, and whole-life performance.
Conduct regular site inspections and verify that the works are progressing in accordance with contractual and technical requirements.
Maintain project momentum and actively resolve issues rather than relying solely on consultants or contractors to drive resolution.

Stakeholder & Authority Management

Act as a key project interface between internal stakeholders, consultants, contractors, operators, and external organizations.
Coordinate requirements with port authorities, municipalities, utility providers, civil defence, customs, landlords, and other relevant government or regulatory entities.
Translate competing stakeholder requirements into practical project decisions.
Prepare clear technical papers, recommendations, presentations, and decision briefs for senior management.
Escalate issues with a clear explanation of the problem, available options, implications, and recommended course of action.

Project Controls & Governance

Maintain accurate project schedules, budgets, risk registers, change logs, action trackers, and project dashboards.
Produce concise and decision-oriented weekly and monthly project reports.
Monitor progress, critical milestones, expenditure, commitments, forecast cost, and key risks.
Maintain appropriate project documentation and ensure decisions and changes are properly recorded.
Support the continuous improvement of project-management procedures, templates, lessons learned, cost databases, and delivery standards.

Commissioning & Closeout

Coordinate testing, commissioning, inspections, snagging, statutory approvals, and operational readiness.
Manage project handover to operations and maintenance teams.
Ensure completion of as-built drawings, O&M manuals, warranties, training records, asset information, and other closeout documentation.
Track defects and outstanding obligations through final completion.
Conduct project closeout reviews and capture lessons learned for future developments.

Candidate Profile

Experience

Approximately 8–12 years of relevant professional experience
, with meaningful responsibility for project delivery.
Demonstrated experience managing infrastructure or capital projects through multiple stages of the project lifecycle.
Experience in one or more of the following is required:
Ports and container terminals
Inland container depots and dry ports
Logistics facilities and freight terminals
Warehouses and industrial developments
Marine and heavy civil infrastructure
Transport infrastructure
Exposure to brownfield or operational environments
where construction must be coordinated around ongoing operations is highly desirable.
Client-side, developer, port-operator, consultant, or strong main-contractor experience will be considered provided the candidate demonstrates genuine project ownership.

Education & Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or another relevant engineering discipline
.
Master’s degree in a relevant field is advantageous.
Industry specific certifications are advantageous.
PMP, PRINCE2, PMI-SP, or equivalent project-management qualification is advantageous but not mandatory.
Knowledge of FIDIC or similar international forms of contract is advantageous.

Technical & Commercial Competencies

The candidate is not expected to personally design every discipline but must have enough engineering judgment to understand, interrogate, and coordinate multidisciplinary projects.
The successful candidate should be comfortable with:
Civil and infrastructure works
Pavements and container-yard development
Drainage and utilities
Buildings and warehouses
MEP and fire/life-safety systems
Port and logistics operational layouts
Marine works and dredging at a working-knowledge level
Material quantities and preliminary cost estimation
Construction methodology and constructability
Project scheduling and critical-path analysis
Tendering and technical bid evaluation
Contract administration and change management
CAPEX development and cost control
Risk identification and mitigation

Competence in tools such as Primavera P6, MS Project, Excel, AutoCAD, Power BI, BIM/Revit, or equivalent systems is advantageous.

High-Volume Operating Model

Establish operating cadences, planning processes, scorecards, and escalation paths.
Translate hiring goals into funnel requirements, capacity plans, and execution priorities.
Maintain a consolidated view of hiring health, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions.

Identify opportunities to standardize and scale the high-volume model across additional hiring areas.

Agency and Vendor Management

Establish clear expectations and scorecards covering submissions, quality, fill rate, time-to-fill, pricing, responsiveness, and corrective action.
Create a consistent process for agency onboarding, performance reviews, escalation, and offboarding.

Automate reporting, funnel tracking, quality monitoring, and partner performance visibility.

Overview

Project Managers independently lead projects across multiple workstreams, owning delivery from planning through completion while balancing scope, timing, budget, quality, and client expectations.

Project Managers bring clarity to complexity. As active delivery leaders, Project Managers apply strong project management, financial, and operational expertise to keep work moving forward, improve how work gets done, and strengthen delivery outcomes. Evaluate and apply new tools, technologies, and AI-enabled ways of working that improve efficiency, visibility, and delivery outcomes.

BAE Systems is seeking a Senior Technical Project Manager to support our work for the U.S. Navy's Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Strategic Systems Programs (SSP) command. This position collaborates with a Program Engineer to lead one of several complex projects within a dynamic, large system-of-systems engineering portfolio, and requires a detail-oriented self-starter who can work effectively with individuals at all levels. Excellent leadership, organization, and communication skills are critical; the strongest candidates will have some systems engineering experience in addition to expert project/program management skills.

Responsibilities Include

Define and manage a master project plan, establish a governance framework, and maintain a weekly work management cadence to ensure timely completion of deliverables and achievement of milestones.
Collaborate with multiple stakeholders to manage all phases of the systems engineering lifecycle—requirements, analysis, design, implementation, testing, and deployment—while ensuring alignment to stakeholder needs.
Provide clear, accurate, and value-added communications to both team members and leadership.
Perform status reporting, issue resolution, and stakeholder management.
Coordinate with other project managers across the portfolio to ensure consistency of processes and deliverables.
Help develop industry-specific delivery accelerators (e.g., templates, best practices, automation tools).
Manage and monitor risks and issues, and develop mitigation plans.
Maintain project collaboration and artifact repository sites.

About BAE Systems and the U.S. Navy’s (USN’s) Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Strategic Systems Programs (SSP)

Our organization has supported the USN’s PAE SSP continually since the command’s inception in the 1950s. PAE SSP developed the first sea-based, underwater-launched Strategic Weapons System (SWS), a defense system that is critical to our national security. PAE SSP has maintained and upgraded the sea-based SWS for more than six decades, and we have been there every step of the way: it is the ultimate stealthy weapons system, and is one leg of the U.S. nuclear triad. Containing over 70% of our nation’s nuclear arsenal, its importance to maintaining world peace cannot be overstated. Development of the Columbia-class submarine—the most advanced nuclear-powered, nuclear-armed submarine ever designed—and the D5LE2 system are underway, and rollout will begin within the next decade. The USN projects this system to be operational through 2084, meaning the program will have a total life span of more than 120 years. This is a truly unique program, and the BAE Systems employees who support it understand that they’re part of an important legacy.

As a decades-long sole-source partner on multiple contracts on behalf of our customer, our program has remarkable stability and is concurrently experiencing significant growth. These factors combine to provide ample opportunity for professional growth and development for capable and talented individuals on our team.

BAE Systems, Inc. is a wholly owned U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, which provides some of the world's most advanced, technology-led defense, aerospace, and security solutions. As one of the top ten defense contractors, we employ a skilled workforce of around 100,000 people in more than 40 countries. We develop, engineer, manufacture, and support products and systems to protect national security and keep people safe.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills

Bachelor's degree or higher

The Role

Reporting to the Director, Business Management Team, the Technical Project Manager is responsible for leading the delivery of complex technology projects and initiatives across the Enterprise Technology Division (ETD).

The role provides end-to-end project leadership for New Policy Proposal (NPP) and capital funded initiatives and acts as the central point of coordination between business stakeholders and ETD delivery teams.

The role requires a strong blend of project management expertise and technical understanding to effectively coordinate activities across multiple technical disciplines and identify delivery impacts arising from changes to project scope, priorities or schedules.

Duties and Responsibilities

Responsibilities of the EL1 may include:

Lead and coordinate complex ICT projects from initiation through delivery, transition and closure, ensuring outcomes are delivered within agreed scope, budget, timeframes and quality expectations.
Work collaboratively with initiating teams to establish an agreed delivery approach, clarify business and technical requirements, define responsibilities and confirm the information, decisions and resources required to commence delivery.
Identify, map and actively manage dependencies across infrastructure, cloud, platforms, networks, cyber security, applications, architecture, service management and operational teams.
Develop and maintain integrated project plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, risk and issue registers, dependency logs, decision records and other project controls.
Provide accurate, timely and evidence-based advice on project progress, expenditure, risks, dependencies, decisions and emerging delivery impacts.
Build productive relationships across business and technical teams.
Assess proposed changes to scope, schedule or priorities and ensure changes are appropriately documented, agreed and approved.
Proactively identify delivery barriers, information gaps and unresolved dependencies, escalating matters where necessary and presenting practical options and recommendations to senior decision-makers.

Job Description:

The Travel Program Manager oversees the day-to-day operation of the firm's travel program and serves as the primary liaison between internal stakeholders and the firm's Travel Management Company (TMC), preferred travel suppliers, and other external travel partners. Working under the direction of the Senior Manager, this role ensures the TMC and supplier network deliver against firm expectations, resolves escalated traveler issues, and supports continuous improvement of the program through data analysis, policy administration, and stakeholder engagement.

Rather than performing day-to-day booking or administrative tasks, the Travel Program Manager directs the TMC and supplier network to execute against firm expectations. Success is measured by the strength of vendor and internal relationships, traveler satisfaction and compliance, and the operational effectiveness of the program. A hybrid work arrangement is available for this position.

A career at Nixon Peabody is the opportunity to do work that matters. It’s the chance to use your knowledge to shape what’s ahead. To share, to innovate, to learn at a firm that taps the power of collective thinking.

We’ve created a dynamic, energizing environment that promotes success for our clients and each other. We offer fast growth, connectedness and training in business as well as law. And our rigorous standards assure you are part of a diverse team of top talent at every turn.

If you’re someone who’s looking toward the future, we’d love to hear from you.

Location:
Rochester, NY; Albany, NY; Boston, MA; Providence, RI; New York City, NY; Long Island, NY; Washington, DC

Reporting Relationships:
This position will report to the Senior Manager, Procurement and Travel

Essential Job Responsibilities:

Vendor Relationship & Program Oversight

Serve as the firm's day-to-day relationship contact for the TMC and key travel suppliers (airlines, hotels, ground transportation, and related providers), holding partners accountable to service levels and firm expectations.
Participate in and help lead recurring business reviews with the TMC and preferred suppliers; support the Senior Manager in translating outcomes into program improvements.
Act as the escalation point for travel-related issues raised by attorneys, business professionals, and travel arrangers; drive issues to resolution through the TMC and supplier network.
Represent the firm at industry briefings, supplier events, and travel program meetings as appropriate

Program Performance & Continuous Improvement

Monitor travel program performance, policy compliance, traveler experience, and supplier performance; identify trends and coordinate corrective action through the TMC.
Analyze firm travel data and industry trends to identify cost-savings opportunities, policy refinements, and program enhancements; present findings and recommendations to the Senior Manager.
Oversee the day-to-day configuration and optimization of the firm's online booking tool, directing the TMC on maintenance, enhancements, and user-experience improvements.
Partner with Finance to ensure travel transaction data flows correctly for client billing and firm reporting; serve as the point of contact for data-integrity and reconciliation issues.

Policy, Communications & Traveler Enablement

Administer the firm's travel policy: monitor compliance, recommend updates to the Senior Manager, and interpret policy for stakeholders.
Develop communications, guidance, and training resources for firm travelers and travel arrangers; coordinate with the TMC to deliver booking-tool training and onboarding.
Serve as a subject-matter resource on travel program questions, including duty of care and traveler safety in coordination with the TMC.

Group & Event Travel Oversight

Provide oversight and coordination for group travel and firm events, directing the TMC and suppliers to execute logistics and ensuring firm requirements are met.
Support the establishment and management of agreements for lodging, ground transportation, and related services in support of firm events and meetings.

Supplier Agreements & Negotiation

Support negotiations with travel suppliers to secure favorable pricing, terms, and service commitments; partner with the Senior Manager, Procurement, and Legal on contract execution.
Provide input on the firm's preferred supplier program, recommending additions, changes, or consolidations based on spend, traveler needs, and market conditions.

Program Documentation

Document program standards, procedures, and vendor playbooks to support continuity, succession, and consistent execution.

To perform this job successfully, you must be able to perform each essential job responsibility listed above, satisfactorily, with or without reasonable accommodation. Nixon Peabody retains the right to change or assign other duties to this position. The requirements listed below are representative of the skills and abilities required.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Hospitality, Finance, or a related field preferred. Relevant work experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
4+ years of corporate travel program or related experience, ideally in a professional services or similarly complex environment.
Experience working closely with a Travel Management Company and preferred supplier programs.
Experience supporting supplier negotiations and administering corporate travel policy.
Experience analyzing travel spend and program data.
Global Business Travel Association (GBTA) certification or similar (e.g., GTP, GLP) a plus.
Strong relationship-management and stakeholder-communication skills, with the ability to hold vendors accountable and navigate internal partnerships across all levels of the firm.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to translate data into recommendations.
Sound judgment and the ability to distinguish between issues to resolve directly, escalate, or delegate to the TMC/supplier.
Working knowledge of the corporate travel ecosystem, including TMC operations, online booking tools, and supplier dynamics.
Proactive, solutions-oriented approach with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced professional services environment.

Nixon Peabody is committed to creating a fair workplace and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. At Vasion, our mission is to make digital transformation attainable for everyone. We build cloud-native enterprise software that empowers organizations to automate workflows, eliminate paper, and operate smarter. We are scaling fast, we do not do conventional, and we hire people who think the same way.

About The Role

Vasion is adopting a Product Development Life Cycle, a cross-company operating model designed to bring just enough structure to how we build and ship software. As a Program Manager on the PDLC team, you will be one of the people who makes it real.

This is not a coordination role. You will not be tracking status and scheduling syncs. You will be embedded across engineering and product management teams as a practitioner, coach, and change agent helping teams not just follow the PDLC, but understand it, trust it, and work inside it naturally.

You will split your time between two things: operating the PDLC across active programs day-to-day, and helping build and improve the framework itself. Your perspective from inside the teams will actively shape how the system evolves. Vasion's engineering organization is also moving toward agent-native development, which means genuine curiosity about AI is part of the job.

What You Will Do

PDLC Adoption and Change Enablement

Operate as an embedded PDLC practitioner, modeling the framework and helping cross-functional partners understand why it exists and how to use it
Coach engineering and product management team members on PDLC practices by meeting them where they are, not where the playbook says they should be
Build trust through consistency, follow-through, and genuine partnership, not process authority
Communicate the value of the PDLC to engineering clearly and often: reduced context-switching, clearer scope handoffs, fewer rebuilds, better predictability

PDLC Framework Contribution and Development

Partner with the VP of PgM to build, document, and refine processes, templates, stage gate criteria, and governance standards
Develop and maintain playbooks and documentation that make the PDLC accessible across Product Management and Engineering
Translate on-the-ground experience into framework improvements

Own the full lifecycle of assigned programs from Discovery through Grow: scope, timelines, milestones, dependencies, and deliverables at every stage
Build program plans that give Product Management, Engineering, Design, QA, and Go-to-Market a shared view of what is happening, what is next, and who owns what
Stay ahead of risks and blockers; bring well-reasoned options to the VP before problems compound
Facilitate kick-offs, stage gate reviews, cross-functional syncs, and retrospectives to drive clear outcomes and documented next steps every time

Cross-Functional Alignment and Communication

Serve as the day-to-day coordination point between Product Management, Engineering, Design, QA, and Go-to-Market for programs in your portfolio
Surface and resolve cross-team misalignments and dependency conflicts before they impact delivery

Reporting and Documentation

Treat documentation as a core part of program quality in order to make programs reproducible, learnable, and increasingly agent-ready

Requirements

5-8 years of program management experience in software, at the program level across multiple teams
Cross-functional programs through multiple phases of a product or software development lifecycle
Embedded directly within engineering and/or product management teams, not a centralized PMO
Participated in or drove a process or operating model change
Fluency with Atlassian (J

Job Description

This Opportunity

The Senior Power Delivery Project Manager provides technical, administrative, and commercial project management leadership for the development, execution, delivery, and monitoring of Power Delivery projects, including electric transmission, distribution, and substation initiatives, within a defined geographic region, utility client base, or technical discipline. Supports utility capital programs and Power Delivery portfolios by ensuring all responsibilities across the full project lifecycle—including proposal development, project planning and startup, engineering coordination, procurement, construction execution, schedule and cost control, reporting, and project closeout—are executed, documented, and audited in accordance with WSP project management standards, Power Delivery best practices, and client requirements. Provides practical leadership, process improvement, and innovative solutions to address schedule, cost, risk, quality, and stakeholder management challenges within a dynamic, regulated, and evolving Power Delivery and energy infrastructure environment

This position will be based out of New Orleans, LA with the ability to work remotely from any mutually acceptable location in the region. You must have the ability to travel to a WSP and/or Client office for periodic face to face meetings.

As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, WSP now brings world-class expertise in power delivery and project management with the recent acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. Our vision is to be the preeminent pure-play global consulting firm for the world’s energy transition. And we need your help.

Your Impact

Provide Power Delivery project management leadership for large‑scale and complex utility infrastructure projects, ensuring clear task ownership, schedule accountability, and delivery milestones across transmission, distribution, and substation scopes; prepare and manage project budgets, forecasts, margins, KPIs, earned value, hours and expenses, monitor external risks and contingencies, and ensure contractual compliance and successful delivery of assigned Power Delivery project portfolios.
Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and communication strategies for utility clients, internal leadership, engineering teams, contractors, and regulators, maintaining strong relationships and providing timely reporting on project status, risks, and performance. [
Provide guidance during pursuit, initiation, and project startup phases, supporting Go/No‑Go decisions, contract and commercial reviews, pricing strategies, delivery risk assessments, and mitigation planning for Power Delivery and utility capital projects
Participate in and support the technical and commercial aspects of contract negotiations, client presentations, scope alignment discussions, and project execution meetings with IOUs, IPPs, cooperatives, and public power clients.
Actively lead and enforce appropriate technical and constructability reviews, ensuring selection of qualified engineering and discipline leads, adherence to QA/QC programs, and compliance with utility standards and WSP project quality plans.
Provide written and verbal technical input to multi‑disciplinary Power Delivery project teams and contribute strategic, risk‑informed advisory guidance to clients on schedule, cost, constructability, and execution strategy.
Mentor and coach project managers, engineers, and support staff, supporting career development, performance improvement, and leadership growth within the Power Delivery organization.
Manage, evaluate, and provide performance leadership to assigned staff, ensuring alignment with project objectives, safety expectations, and delivery standards
Ensure timely updates and governance compliance for project management systems and documentation, including Risk Registers (REF/RMP), Project Management Plans (PMP), Quality Plans (QP), Project Safety Plans (PSP), and Communications Plans
Facilitate and lead project kick‑off, safety, and execution alignment meetings with key internal and external stakeholders to establish roles, responsibilities, and delivery expectations.
Coordinate with area managers, technical leads, and resource managers to address staffing, subcontracting, and specialty support needs in a timely manner across Power Delivery programs.
Maintain regular client communications, including monthly progress reporting, safety performance, major risks/issues, and scope or budget impacts, reinforcing WSP’s role as a trusted Power Delivery advisor.
Participate in and lead problem project and recovery reviews, conducting root‑cause analysis, identifying corrective actions, and developing project recovery and mitigation plans
Ensure consistent project reporting and governance updates to clients, technical leadership, and business unit managers, proactively identifying emerging scope, schedule, cost, or risk issues.
Monitor and manage accounts receivable (AR), unbilled revenue, cash flow, and invoicing, coordinating with project accounting and finance teams to resolve issues and maintain financial health of Power Delivery projects.
Complete formal project closeout activities, including financial closeout, documentation archiving, client acceptance, and lessons‑learned workshops to support continuous improvement. [
Remain current on project management best practices, PMAP methodologies, utility delivery trends, and Power Delivery industry standards
Collaborate with cross‑disciplinary professionals to deliver integrated, future‑ready power delivery solutions, strengthening WSP’s position as a trusted advisor to utility clients.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision‑making regarding company funds, client commitments, project risks, and professional conduct, in accordance with WSP’s Code of Conduct and corporate policies.
Perform additional responsibilities as required

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical), Engineering Technology, Physical Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience within an A/E/C, utility, EPC, or power delivery consulting environment.
12+ years of progressive post‑education experience in a project management or senior technical leadership role, preferably supporting power delivery, transmission & distribution (T&D), substation, or utility capital projects.
Highly proficient understanding of the project delivery lifecycle within the A/E/C and utility industries, including proposal development, project initiation, engineering coordination, procurement support, construction execution, commissioning, and project closeout, with a strong background in Power Delivery project management
Advanced analytical and organizational skills with demonstrated business and commercial acumen, enabling effective integration of project controls, financial performance, risk management, and client objectives.
Advanced proficiency in critical thinking, risk‑based decision‑making, and problem‑solving, including performing project management assessments, schedule and cost evaluations, forecasting, and scenario analysis to optimize Power Delivery project outcomes.
Advanced interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to engage effectively, persuasively, and professionally with executive leadership, utility clients (IOUs, IPPs, Co‑Ops, Munis), subcontractors, consultants, and internal teams.
Demonstrated self‑leadership and accountability, with strong attention to detail, quality, multitasking, and adaptability in a fast‑paced Power Delivery and utility project environment.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while providing technical guidance, mentoring, and leadership to mid‑level and senior project staff, with strict adherence to QA/QC, safety, and delivery standards.
Advanced proficiency in technical writing, project documentation, office automation, and project management software, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), scheduling tools, and Power Delivery PM platforms.
Strong experience managing the review, approval, and coordination of discipline‑specific deliverables, technical reports, scopes of work, and execution plans within a multi‑project, multi‑disciplinary Power Delivery portfolio.
Demonstrated ability to influence and gain cooperation from a broad range of stakeholders, including senior leadership, utility clients, subcontractors, consultants, and matrixed internal teams, without formal authority.
Proven commitment to workplace health, safety, and environmental performance, including adherence to WSP safety programs, drug/alcohol policies, and harassment‑free workplace standards.
Strong ability to adapt to changing project demands, including flexible schedules, outage‑driven work, and evolving client priorities common in Power Delivery and utility capital programs.
Willingness to support occasional travel to client sites, regional offices, and project locations as required to support Power Delivery project execution and client engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Essential project management certification (e.g., PMP, CAP-M).

Help protect the U.S. homeland. You'll join a team of Research, Development, Test & Evaluation (RDT&E) professionals who identify, integrate, and assess technologies for the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Defense as a core member of Amentum's Center of Excellence for Counter Unmanned Systems (C-UxS)

As a Research Analyst, you will turn all-source C-UxS information into analytical products that directly shape DHS and DoD technology acquisition and the development of tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). You'll work with Amentum, government, vendors, subject matter experts, and other industry partners. Your findings will reach senior decision makers.

What You'll Do

Analysis and Threat Assessment

Analyze structured and unstructured UxS movement data, geospatial sensor information, and supplementary intelligence sources to develop actionable analytical products.
Brief key decision-makers on UxS movement trends, entities, areas of interest, and evolving threat patterns through reports, presentations, and research projects.
Conduct predictive and anticipatory analysis to identify emerging UxS threats, forecast potential operational activities, and assess likely changes in adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures.
Identify patterns, anomalies, and indicators of potential future UxS activity by integrating historical movement data, geospatial information, environmental conditions, and other relevant intelligence sources.
Develop threat forecasts and risk assessments that identify potential vulnerabilities, emerging operational challenges, and areas requiring enhanced surveillance, detection, or mitigation capabilities.
Apply trend analysis, pattern-of-life assessments, and temporal and geospatial modeling to anticipate changes in UxS employment, operating environments, and threat behavior.

Predictive Analytics and Operational Decision Support

Develop and apply predictive analytical models, statistical forecasting techniques, and AI-enabled analytical tools to assess potential UxS activities, operational trends, and emerging threats.
Conduct anticipatory assessments that evaluate plausible future threat scenarios, identify early warning indicators, and provide decision-makers with actionable recommendations.
Establish and monitor indicators and warnings (I&W) to support early identification of emerging UxS threats, evolving capabilities, and changes in operational activity.
Perform scenario-based analysis and forecasting to evaluate potential threat developments, operational vulnerabilities, and C-UxS capability requirements.
Translate predictive assessments into operational recommendations that support proactive resource allocation, sensor placement, technology acquisition, and TTP development.
Evaluate the accuracy, reliability, and operational utility of predictive models through historical validation, performance metrics, and continuous analytical refinement.

Technology Assessment and Capability Development

Partner with government and industry stakeholders to define research objectives, data collection methodologies, analytical requirements, and reporting standards.
Transform analytical findings into actionable recommendations that guide C-UxS technology development, acquisition, selection, and operational employment.
Develop and manage multi-phase technology implementation roadmaps across business units, translating functional requirements into actionable system configurations.
Perform due diligence on emerging AI, machine learning, and other advanced technologies that can enhance C-UxS detection, tracking, classification, and analytical capabilities.
Identify anticipated capability gaps by evaluating projected threat evolution against existing and planned C-UxS technologies, operational concepts, and system performance.
Support technology investment and acquisition decisions by forecasting future operational requirements and assessing the effectiveness of potential C-UxS solutions against emerging threats.

Research, Modeling, and Program Support

Apply operations research, systems analysis, statistical modeling, and quantitative methodologies to complex operational and technical challenges.
Support business process improvement initiatives, including performance management, statistical process control, organizational assessment, and regulatory compliance.
Conduct modeling and simulation, strategic planning, operational analysis, and decision support to advance program objectives.
Develop analytical scenarios and simulations to assess potential UxS threat evolution, operational impacts, and the effectiveness of proposed countermeasures.
Assist with program planning and oversight, exercise development and execution, and program evaluation.
Support system-level analysis and integration activities, including assessments of emerging threats, system vulnerabilities, and operational effectiveness.
Provide technical assessment and evaluation support that complements government technical experts in applying acquisition initiatives and research, development, test, and evaluation (RDT&E) activities to DHS mission requirements.

Leadership, Collaboration, and Compliance

Communicate complex analytical findings, predictive assessments, and operational recommendations to senior government and industry leadership.
Conduct all activities in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and restrictions governing information collection, intelligence analysis, and law enforcement activities within the United States.
Supervise analytical and technical staff as assigned.
Travel domestically and internationally as required.

Minimum Qualifications

Must have an active Secret US Government clearance. Note: US Citizenship is required to obtain a Secret Clearance
Ability to pass DHS Entry on Duty (EOD) requirements and maintain Public Trust suitability
Bachelor's degree and 10 years of all-source intelligence analysis and production that includes DHS and/or DoD experience.
Experience with commercial or government GIS tools (ArcGIS or similar) and with OSINT and other data sources across the intelligence cycle
Track record of producing high-quality deliverables for senior policymakers, including complex written products and formal or informal briefings, independently or as part of a team
Strong research, analytical, interpersonal, organizational, and written and verbal communication skills, with close attention to detail and the ability to anticipate customer needs
Ability to work independently and collaboratively

Preferred Qualifications

Active Top Secret clearance and active Public Trust designation
Knowledge of C-UxS methods, industry leaders, and U.S. Government authorities
Understanding of sUAS threats and the electronic and communications systems, components, and materials relevant to DHS missions
Familiarity with DHS, DoD, or other law enforcement C-UxS efforts over the past five years
Experience with DHS GII, Aerial Armor, Hidden Level, or similar UAS detection and monitoring services

new_jobs.description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.
Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

About the Opportunity

We are seeking an exceptional emerging strategy professional to help shape the future of a >$3B global consumer electronics business.
Our business spans the full consumer value chain—from consumer insights, product strategy, design, and development through marketing, sales, and supply chain. This creates a unique opportunity to influence both long-term business direction and the product portfolio choices that drive growth and profitability.
This role is ideal for someone who combines structured strategic thinking, exceptional written communication, analytical curiosity, and a highly collaborative working style.

The successful candidate will be comfortable starting with an ambiguous business question, working across functions to define the problem, developing frameworks and hypotheses, and identifying the data and insights needed to test potential solutions. Equally important, they must be able to distill complex strategies and analyses into clear, persuasive written narratives that support decisions at the executive and Board of Directors level.
We are particularly interested in candidates with a foundation in top-tier management consulting who are eager to move from advising businesses to directly influencing strategic choices and outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Problem Framing & Hypothesis Development
Lead the structured definition of complex, often ambiguous business problems, translating broad strategic questions into clear issues, analytical frameworks, and testable hypotheses.
Collaborate closely with functional leaders and subject matter experts to develop an understanding of the business, challenge assumptions, and identify the most important questions to answer.
Apply hypothesis-driven problem-solving techniques to focus analytical efforts on the highest-impact issues.
Identify relevant internal and external data sources, determine what evidence is needed, and develop practical approaches to testing hypotheses.
Synthesize quantitative and qualitative findings, refining hypotheses as new information emerges.
Balance analytical rigor with pragmatism, recognizing when sufficient evidence exists to support a strategic recommendation.
Executive Communication & Strategic Storytelling
Translate complex strategic thinking, business analyses, and cross-functional inputs into concise, compelling written narratives for senior executives and the Board of Directors.
Develop high-quality strategy memoranda, executive briefs, decision papers, and strategic recommendations that make complicated issues easy to understand.
Structure communications around clear conclusions, supporting evidence, strategic implications, and decisions required.
Distill large amounts of information into the essential insights, trade-offs, and recommendations without losing critical nuance.
Tailor communications to different audiences, from working-level teams to executive leadership and the Board.
Establish a high standard for clarity, precision, logical flow, and persuasive business writing.
Business Unit & Product Portfolio Strategy
Support development of the business unit's multi-year strategy, including growth opportunities, competitive positioning, market priorities, and investment choices.
Partner with Product Management, Consumer Insights, Finance, and other functions to develop and refine product portfolio strategies.
Evaluate consumer needs, market dynamics, competitive trends, product economics, and portfolio performance to inform strategic decisions.
Develop business cases and strategic scenarios to evaluate growth opportunities, portfolio alternatives, and resource allocation.
Connect product portfolio recommendations to broader business objectives, financial performance, and long-term competitive advantage.
Collaborative Discovery & Cross-Functional Engagement
Build trusted relationships across Product Management, Design, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Finance, and Supply Chain.
Approach new strategic challenges with curiosity, humility, and a genuine desire to learn from those closest to the business.
Facilitate working sessions that bring structure to complex discussions, surface diverse perspectives, and establish shared understanding of problems and opportunities.
Work collaboratively with subject matter experts to identify relevant information, test assumptions, and develop fact-based conclusions.
Constructively challenge existing thinking while remaining open to alternative perspectives and new evidence.
Build alignment and influence decisions through strong reasoning, credibility, and collaboration rather than positional authority.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Finance, or a related discipline.
Typically 2–5 years of experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, or a similarly rigorous analytical environment.
Outstanding written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to translate complex business issues into concise, logically structured, executive-ready memoranda and recommendations.
Strong command of structured problem-solving methodologies, including issue definition, analytical frameworks, hypothesis development, and hypothesis testing.
Demonstrated resourcefulness in identifying, gathering, and analyzing data to answer complex business questions, including situations where information is incomplete or difficult to access.
Ability to synthesize qualitative and quantitative information into actionable strategic insights.
Highly collaborative working style, strong listening skills, intellectual humility, and the ability to learn quickly from cross-functional experts.
Strong business judgment, intellectual curiosity, and comfort navigating ambiguity.

Preferred

Experience at a leading strategy consulting firm such as McKinsey, Bain, BCG, or a comparable organization.
Experience developing executive-level strategy documents, investment recommendations, or Board-facing materials.
Exposure to consumer electronics, technology, consumer products, or other innovation-driven businesses.
Experience in growth strategy, product portfolio strategy, corporate strategy, or commercial due diligence.
MBA or advanced degree is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will:
Bring clarity and structure to ambiguous strategic questions, helping leadership focus on the issues that matter most.
Build effective partnerships with business leaders and functional experts, demonstrating curiosity and credibility during the discovery process.
Develop thoughtful, evidence-based hypotheses and know how to efficiently find the information needed to validate or challenge them.
Produce exceptionally clear strategy memoranda that enable executives and Board members to quickly understand complex issues, evaluate trade-offs, and make informed decisions.
Contribute meaningfully to business unit and product portfolio strategies that influence long-term growth and competitiveness.

About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few.
